### US Map Heat Map

```{r}

# 1. Input your data
df <- data.frame(
  state = c("Iowa", "Michigan", "Minnesota", "New York", "Ohio", "Pennsylvania", "Wisconsin"),
  n = c(1, 1, 16, 2, 1, 1, 9))

# 2. Plot the heat map
plot_usmap(
  data = df, 
  values = "n", 
  exclude = c("AK", "HI"), # Excludes non-Lower 48 states
  color = "white",         # State border color
  size = 0.3
) +
  scale_fill_continuous(
    low = "#fee0d2", 
    high = "#de2d26", 
    name = "Count (n)",
    na.value = "#f0f0f0") +
  labs(
    title = "Lower 48 State Map",
    subtitle = "Concentration of counts by state") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5))
```

### Producer Experience Graphs

```{r}

# 1. Create the dataset
df <- data.frame(
  category = c("Individual housing only", "Social housing"),
  count = c(19, 12)
) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = round(count / sum(count) * 100, 1),
    # Combine label, count, and percentage for the chart key/labels
    label = paste0(count, " (", percentage, "%)")
  )

# Donut chart variant
ggplot(df, aes(x = 2, y = count, fill = category)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "white", size = 1.2) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  xlim(0.5, 2.5) + # Controls the inner hole size
  # Centered total label inside the hole
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0, label = paste0("Total\n", sum(df$count)), 
           size = 6, fontface = "bold", color = "#333333") +
  # Slice labels
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "black",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Individual housing only" = "#a52a2a", 
                               "Social housing" = "#cd5c5c")) +
  labs(
    title = "Housing Breakdown",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

```

```{r}


# 1. Create the dataset
df <- data.frame(
  category = c(
    "No transition experienced",
    "Reverted from social to individual housing",
    "Switched from individual housing to social"
  ),
  count = c(23, 5, 3)
) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = round(count / sum(count) * 100, 1),
    # Combine count and percentage on one single line
    label = paste0(count, " (", percentage, "%)")
  )

# Preserve order
df$category <- factor(df$category, levels = df$category)

# 2. Define custom yellow palette
yellow_palette <- c(
  "No transition experienced" = "#d4a373",                    # Warm Honey / Amber
  "Reverted from social to individual housing" = "#ffb703",   # Bright Yellow
  "Switched from individual housing to social" = "#ffe6a7"    # Soft Light Yellow
)

# 3. Plot the Donut Chart
ggplot(df, aes(x = 2, y = count, fill = category)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "white", size = 1.2) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  xlim(0.5, 2.5) +
  # Slice labels in one line
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "black",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = yellow_palette) +
  labs(
    title = "Housing Transitions Breakdown",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))
```
